translation: I, from youth, received the [teaching] of Nanjing and Suwen from Master Zhang Yuansu of the Yishui school. Having lectured and recited for a long time, I gradually gained some attainment. From middle age onward, having encountered many affairs and treated many cases in their diagnosis and treatment, I remained unconfused. I once wrote a discourse, "Differentiation of Internal and External Injury," to testify against the errors of the world in the use of medicine. The hills and valleys changed [in my life journey], and suddenly I entered old age; my spirit and mind having become sluggish and lazy in speech, this discourse has lain bound and put on the shelf for sixteen years. My honored master, Fan of Kunlun, generously praised and encouraged it, and repeatedly used [the words] "to save the living" — saying that if this book were truly put into circulation, so that the people of the world might not die untimely, this too is the business of a humane gentleman to rescue people and benefit things. Even if I exhaust myself in authorship and fritter away my vital strength, and die once the book is finished, would that not be better than living without benefit? I respectfully received his words and, mustering my strength despite illness, completed it. Although it is not yet complete and prepared, it briefly answers the compassionate will of my honored master. My master is a descendant of Grand Academician Song Wenzheng. On the Double Ninth Festival in the year of Ding-wei, inscribed by Dongyuan Laozi [the Old Man of the Eastern Plain], Li Gao, styled Mingzhi.
